note: Leg plan per research/humanoid_legs.md and Kimi round 2/3. The 3D legs are the Berkeley Humanoid Lite biped (CC-BY-SA-4.0) scaled to InMoov size: the v2 full-size concept. Kimi is researching InMoov-specific leg designs. 'match' is a regex on URDF link names.

stages.title: Learn to walk in simulation
stages.text: Train a walking policy for this exact robot in MuJoCo, starting from the ToddlerBot and Open Duck code. No hardware needed yet.

stages.title: Build the real walker
stages.text: If the torso build is on schedule and at least C$400 is left: a small 0.62 m servo walker, about C$390, to prove the walking code on real hardware.

stages.title: Full-size legs under the InMoov
stages.text: The legs shown here: 12 brushless joints strong enough to carry the ~9 kg InMoov upper body, around C$150-250 per joint. That's the next budget.

parts.name: Hips
parts.actuator: Full-size (shown): brushless actuator + printed cycloidal gearbox per joint. Small walker: STS3250 pitch, STS3215 roll/yaw.
parts.made: Printed PETG pelvis and hip brackets

parts.name: Knees
parts.actuator: Full-size: brushless + cycloidal (the knee carries the most load). Small walker: STS3250.

parts.name: Ankles + feet
parts.actuator: Full-size: brushless + cycloidal. Small walker: STS3250 pitch, STS3215 roll.
parts.made: Printed feet with TPU soles for grip

parts.name: Pelvis + balance
parts.actuator: BNO085 IMU for balance, battery, motor drivers; bolts under the InMoov torso
parts.made: Printed torso; shares the main robot's computer and cameras
